title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། དབུ་མ། ཞ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 100)
shelf_note: Derge woodblock folio of a Madhyamaka commentary (sub-commentary on MMK ch. 8, agent and action, quoting 'ཡིན་པར་གྱུར་ལ་བྱ་བ་མེད། །བྱེད་པ་པོ་ཡང་ལས་མེད་འགྱུར།'); belongs in the dbu ma section of the Tengyur.

tr_errors_A.english: because this follows the other previous half-verse
tr_errors_A.problem: 'other' is a stray word; གོང་མ་ཤོས is the preceding (upper) half-verse; sense otherwise right and the lemma is correctly marked as a quoted statement

tr_errors_A.english: in order to set it up as an example
tr_errors_A.problem: ཕྱིར་རོ here gives the reason in a quoted syllogism ('because it is set up as the example'), rendered as purpose

tr_errors_B.english: This first half of the verse follows what was already explained, so it does not need further explanation.
tr_errors_B.problem: The verse half just quoted is said to need no explanation because it follows (parallels) the preceding half-verse; B calls it 'this first half' and loses that it is a quoted lemma from the base commentary being explicated

tr_errors_B.english: To set this up as an example, there is an inference, a challenge, and a response.
tr_errors_B.problem: The reason clause closes the quoted inference; B turns it into a purpose clause governing a new sentence, blurring the syllogism's structure

tr_errors_B.english: was used to prove the reason and the example
tr_errors_B.problem: the thesis is established by statements of reason and example; the reason and example are not what is proved (recurs several times)

tr_errors_B.english: If it is established, there is no action.
tr_errors_B.problem: ཡིན་པར་གྱུར (sadbhūta, an existent/real one) rendered as a conditional 'if it is established'; recoverable but less exact

other.note: B's <summary> claims the page 'explains how established entities cannot undergo new actions because the action would be redundant or logically inconsistent' — no such argument is on this page, which only maps the verse lines onto parallel inferences

pages.prefer_reason: Both get the agent/action theses right, but A correctly treats the 'no need to explain' line as a quoted lemma about the preceding half-verse and keeps the syllogism structure, while B misreads that line and its summary invents an argument.

book_verdict: A genuine Derge Tengyur Madhyamaka folio with a clean transcription; both English versions are serviceable on the doctrinal theses, A more exact on the commentarial structure.
